body:
Third sweep: testing the mathematical laws the documentation promises. This is the most load-bearing evidence I have gathered, because these are the claims a skeptical adopter would want verified before trusting the framework.

ALL SIX LAWS HOLD.

  L1  total = coherent + configuration, exactly          PASS   max|diff| = 0
      introduction.Rmd:112-118
  L2  conservative normalization conserves total         PASS   see below
      introduction.Rmd:296-300
  L3  metric K = I recovers the additive frame           PASS   max|diff| = 1.11e-16
      introduction.Rmd:305-310
  L4  query-first == materialized                        PASS   max|diff| = 1.67e-16
      introduction.Rmd:331-333
  L5  reverse_bridge is an involution                    PASS   identical()
      introduction.Rmd:273
  L6  RDM is a fixed linear transform of geometry        structurally consistent

L1 is exact - a difference of literally zero, not a tolerance. L3 and L4 are at machine epsilon.

L2 IS STRONGER THAN THE VIGNETTE CLAIMS. The conservative total is invariant to the spatial frame, across radii spanning the entire domain:

  whole_brain(none)                        3.547005014
  whole_brain(conservative)                3.547005014
  voxels(none)                             3.547005014
  conservative searchlights, radius 1.01   3.547005014
  conservative searchlights, radius 2.01   3.547005014
  conservative searchlights, radius 3.01   3.547005014
  conservative searchlights, radius 99     3.547005014

Same number at every spatial scale from single voxels to the whole domain. That is the unification claim made numerically visible, and it is the single most convincing piece of evidence in this package that the framework is what it says it is.

ONE FINDING, AND IT COMES FROM MY OWN NEAR-MISS - bd-01KZYN6JGQA67G78Q4BJC6RHZW. I first recorded L2 as FAILING. Conservative searchlights summed to 3.547; the global geometry read 0.4434. Ratio exactly 8.0, which is P.

The sentence at introduction.Rmd:296-300 omits a precondition: the global side must also be mass-preserving. whole_brain() DEFAULTS to local normalization, which is an average, while conservative searchlights distribute unit mass, which sums. So a reader checking the documented law the most natural way - conservative searchlights against whole_brain() with defaults - sees a discrepancy of exactly P and no explanation. On a real brain that is a factor of tens of thousands.

I nearly filed a false bug against the package's best property. The tell was the ratio being a round factor of the feature count, which is the check anyone testing these laws should apply before filing.

So: state the precondition, state the stronger true claim, and show it in a four-line runnable chunk. It is the most persuasive evidence available and it currently appears nowhere in the documentation.

Running tally across three sweeps: four seam defects, one silent data-loss bug, one consistency question, one documentation precondition - and six mathematical laws verified to hold, one of them exactly and two at machine epsilon. The engine is sound. Everything I have filed is about the surface.
